# Oska

> A language. What changed in each release is in the changelog.

Oska 1.10.0 (pre-alpha). These docs track `main`. Every page is also served as Markdown: the same path with `.md`. All of them are in [llms-full.txt](https://oskalang.dev/llms-full.txt). The source code is at https://github.com/aparsons/oska. A program is one `.osk` file or a package: an `oska.toml` and modules under `src/`, with `src/main.osk` as the entry and `use pkg.a.b` importing `src/a/b.osk`; see [Packages and modules](https://oskalang.dev/guide/packages.md). `oskac build` compiles a program to an executable for Linux or macOS on any host: `--target` picks the platform (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-x86_64`, `macos-aarch64` or `macos-x86_64`), `--target all` writes all four, and without `--target` it builds for the host, or for `linux-aarch64` on Windows. On Linux and macOS, `oskac run` and `oskac test` compile natively and run the executable, and `--interpret` selects the interpreter, which Windows uses; output, reports and exit codes are the same on both. See [Platform support](https://oskalang.dev/guide/cli-reference.md#platform-support).

## Docs

- [Oska](https://oskalang.dev/index.md): A language. What changed in each release is in the changelog.
- [Changelog](https://oskalang.dev/changelog.md): Every release's notes, newest first.
- [Glossary](https://oskalang.dev/glossary.md)
- [Reference](https://oskalang.dev/reference.md): How Oska works inside, the words it uses, and the decisions and research behind it. To use Oska, start with the guides.

## Machine-readable

- [llms-full.txt](https://oskalang.dev/llms-full.txt): the documentation, as Markdown, in one file
- [search.json](https://oskalang.dev/search.json): the search index
- [sitemap.xml](https://oskalang.dev/sitemap.xml): the canonical URL of every page
- [latest.json](https://oskalang.dev/latest.json): the current version and the installers
